sources.title: Normalized maximum, endpoint and permutation derivations
sources.details: For a normalized nonnegative distribution with n>=2, 1/n<=p_max<=1. c=(p_max-1/n)/(1-1/n)=(n*p_max-1)/(n-1), so c is in [0,1]; uniform gives 0 and a point mass gives 1. For p_max=3/5,n=3: (3/5-1/3)/(1-1/3)=(4/15)/(2/3)=2/5=0.4. The four-decimal 0.2667 and 0.6667 in prose are rounded intermediates, not an exact rational identity. For n=2: (3/5-1/2)/(1-1/2)=(1/10)/(1/2)=1/5=0.2. For n=1 both numerator and denominator are 0: the expression is undefined. For p=[0.99,0.005,0.005], c=0.985 irrespective of which candidate is gold. Permuting p preserves max(p) and n, hence c, while moving the maximum from position 0 to 1. Thus this scalar cannot identify candidate meaning or correctness. With rubric probabilities [0.5,0,0.5], Choice c=(3*0.5-1)/2=0.25. The official ordinal Score formula has modal index m=0, weighted distance=1 and uniform MAD=2/3, giving max(0,1-1/(2/3))=0.
